cards.text: Israel has just been carried off into Assyria (2 Kings 17:23). So the king of Assyria brings in new people and settles them in the towns of Samaria to replace the Israelites. Out with the old neighbors, in with the new.

cards.question: True or false: The king of Assyria brings all the new settlers in Samaria from one single city.

cards.text: They take over Samaria and move right into its towns. But when they first live there, they don't worship the LORD.

cards.question: The new settlers in Samaria don't worship the LORD, so He sends ___ among them, and some of them are killed.

cards.text: LIONS, friend! I'd have crawled back into my old junk drawer and pulled it shut behind me, but the settlers send word to the king of Assyria instead.

cards.question: The settlers tell the king of Assyria why the lions are killing them. What do they say?

answers.text: We don't know what the God of the land requires
Our towns don't have walls to keep them out
The land sat empty and wild for far too long

cards.text: The king of Assyria has a plan. Somebody has to go live there and teach these people the requirements of the God of the land.

cards.question: The king of Assyria wants someone sent back to Samaria to teach the settlers. Who does he command them to send?

answers.text: One of the priests carried off from Samaria
One of the prophets living in Judah
One of his own officials from Assyria

cards.question: The priest comes back and lives in ___, and he begins teaching the settlers how they should worship the LORD.

cards.text: Problem solved, right? Then the story hits us with the word every storyteller hates to read out loud: nevertheless.

cards.question: The priest is teaching the settlers how to worship the LORD. Nevertheless, what do the people of each nation keep doing?
The people of each nation set up their own gods in shrines on the high places. True or false: They build those shrines from scratch themselves.

cards.text: Every group brings its own: Babylon makes Succoth-benoth, Cuth makes Nergal, Hamath makes Ashima, and the Avvites make Nibhaz and Tartak. And the Sepharvites burn their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
Back in Samaria, the new residents do worship the LORD. But that's not the whole picture.

cards.question: True or false: The one priest sent back from exile is the only priest serving in the shrines on the high places of Samaria.
The new residents of Samaria worship the LORD. What else do they do, following the customs of the nations they came from?

answers.text: They serve their own gods too

cards.text: The LORD AND all their old gods, and still at it to this day? That's telling your barber he's the only one while you've got four other barbers booked that same week.

cards.question: The writer says none of the settlers keep the laws the LORD gave the descendants of ___, whom He named Israel.

cards.text: Then the writer looks back at the covenant the LORD made with the Israelites, and what He commanded them.

cards.question: In His covenant with the Israelites, what does the LORD command them first?

answers.text: Do not ever leave the land
Do not trade with the nations

cards.question: Instead, the Israelites are to worship the LORD, who brought them out of ___ with great power and an outstretched arm.

cards.text: He tells them to always keep His laws and never forget the covenant, and then He says it again, and AGAIN: “Do not worship other gods.” Friend, when I set three timers for one batch, that batch is IMPORTANT.

cards.question: The LORD tells the Israelites to worship the LORD their God. What does He promise if they do?

answers.text: He will deliver them from all their enemies
He will give them a king who rules forever
He will send them rain in every season

cards.text: But they would not listen. They kept right on with their former customs.

cards.question: These nations in Samaria worship the LORD but also serve their idols. True or false: Their children and grandchildren finally break the habit.

findings.problem: Most of the choice cards in stop 1 can only be answered by luck. Card 1 says only "new people," so card 2 (one city or many) can't be reasoned out. Card 4 (lions, bears or snakes) and card 9 (Bethel, Jericho or Hebron) are pure recall. Nothing before card 12 hints at who built the shrines. That makes 4 of the 7 choice cards discovery questions. Only cards 6, 8 and 11 are informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The question says the king wants someone "sent back to Samaria." Only someone who came from Samaria can be sent back there. That rules out the prophet from Judah and the official from Assyria, and points to the one answer that says "carried off from Samaria."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: "Every group brings its own" suggests the settlers carried their gods with them from home. 2 Kings 17:29 says they made their own gods in the cities where they had settled. The card should say "makes," the word the text uses.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "Back in Samaria" says the story left Samaria and is now returning. Every scene in 2 Kings 17:24-32 takes place in Samaria. Card 13 only named the gods each group made there, so nothing in the passage moves away.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "Still at it to this day" (2 Kings 17:34) already tells the baker that the habit never stops. That gives away card 12, which asks whether their children and grandchildren finally break the habit (2 Kings 17:41).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The walkthrough leaves out the writer's key judgment in 2 Kings 17:34: "None of them worship the LORD." Verses 32-33 say the settlers worshiped the LORD, and verse 34 says that worship doesn't count. Card 5 covers only the laws they don't keep, so the baker never sees this turn in the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Both stops follow the same shape. Each opens with a true or false card and closes with a true or false card, with multiple choice and fill in the blank alternating in between (stop 1: TF, FB, MC, MC, FB, MC, TF; stop 2: TF, MC, FB, MC, FB, MC, TF).

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
